heading: On harmful prompts, aligned and base models differ mostly at the first few tokens
definition: the difference between aligned and base models (per-token KL) on harmful prompts sits mostly in the first few response positions.
summary: One independent study reproduces this early-token pattern in KL divergence from the base model for six aligned models from the Llama, Gemma and Qwen families, but shows it only in figures, without numbers for how much of the KL falls early. A diffusion-model study gives an analogue under left-to-right decoding; other reports compare different model pairs, use proxies or are theory, and models above 10B remain untested.

suggested_status.by_scale: 1-10B: R2 for the qualitative positional pattern only, resting on one independent preprint whose per-position KL evidence is figure-only (arXiv:2601.19231 across Llama, Gemma and Qwen). 10-100B: untested after checks. versions.V3.studies_by_size still shows 10-100B: 2, built before the checks. The 10-100B rows shown in the V3 pack are arXiv:2401.17256#r3 (Safe-13B versus harmfully fine-tuned Unsafe-7B), which now has no V3 verdict, and arXiv:2605.08930#r1 and #r2 (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B SInternal variants versus the base reasoning model), which are rows-only, NOT A TEST OF V3 and cannot_determine. arXiv:2610.22467#f0 (initial versus recursively distilled Qwen3 14B) fits no version. <1B: ?. The only result here is a system-prompt proxy (arXiv:2605.15239#P1). Toy and >100B: untested.
suggested_status.reason: An independent group reports aligned/unaligned per-token KL profiles on harmful prompts. They show the qualitative early-position pattern for Llama-2-7B, Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Gemma-7B, Gemma-2-9B and Qwen3-4B (arXiv:2601.19231#r37, #r39, #r41, #r43, #r45, #r47). These profiles are figure-only, and no numerical cumulative-KL fraction is given. Every counts key quoted here was built before the checks. The counts are consistent with independence: versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original=0, and the author lists show no author of arXiv:2601.19231 shared with an original. versions.V3.verdicts.supports.studies=10 and versions.V3.verdicts.limits_scope.studies=2 still include V3 verdicts that the checks set to none (arXiv:2606.12342, arXiv:2401.17256, arXiv:2511.12155, arXiv:2502.04602). arXiv:2509.23286 gives a diffusion analogue (LLaDA-Instruct and LLaDA-1.5 versus LLaDA-Base). Its V3 support holds only for left-to-right decoding (#r16, #r19). Its confidence-based and random-order rows (#r17, #r18, #r20, #r21) index generation steps, not response positions, so they are cannot_determine for V3. arXiv:2401.17256#r2 and #r3 compare Safe-7B and Safe-13B with a harmfully fine-tuned Unsafe-7B, not an aligned model with its pretrained base. After checks they carry no V3 verdict. arXiv:2605.15239#P1 is only a Qwen3-0.6B system-prompt proxy. Coverage keys: versions.V3.studies_by_size and versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.measurement.by_size. Both show 10-100B: 2 from before the checks. The packs do not show which studies that entry counts; none of the 10-100B rows named in by_scale is a V3 test after the checks. The packs do not name the records behind versions.V3.reader_said_tested_verdict_did_not=12 or versions.V3.tested_not_extracted=1. A search of the packs for per-position KL rows and findings that carry no V3 verdict found one new set of aligned-versus-own-pretrained-base profiles on harmful prompts, all for a model trained to deepen safety: arXiv:2509.23286#r22 to #r24 compare A2D-aligned LLaDA-1.5 with LLaDA-Base on the same 150 harmful BeaverTails prompts (figure-only). The verdict reads these rows as the study's deepening intervention, bearing on V7 (where it reads KL as staying large across steps), not V3. Otherwise the nearest record is already in this synthesis: arXiv:2511.12155, whose V3 verdict the checks set to none. Under normal decoding on HEx-PHI, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct versus base KL is about 1.8 at early positions and 0.5 late (#r11), and #r9 pairs Llama-3.1-8B base with Llama-3-8B-Instruct. Neither row defines an opening window or gives a cumulative share, and the checks read both as cannot_determine. arXiv:2505.16186 is tested but has no V3 verdict: its rows compare safety-trained R1-7B and R1-8B models with the base reasoning model on unsafe queries and are figure-only and cannot_determine (#R1 to #R4). arXiv:2503.03710 (#K01, #K02, #K06, #K07), arXiv:2606.00160#f0, arXiv:2602.04896#f0 (shares authors with an original), arXiv:2505.17122#f0 (benign instructions), arXiv:2610.22467#f0 and arXiv:2605.08930#r1, #r2 compare a further-tuned, steered or distilled model with its starting model; all are figure-only or give no numbers. arXiv:2505.08054#R12 measures KL on FalseReject refusal responses, its training distribution, and its verdict reads it as not V3. arXiv:2601.19231#f0 reports the same early concentration for its aligned/unaligned pairs on benign SAMSum data. arXiv:2511.12155#f0 concerns aligned-versus-base KL under its own contrastive decoding. The only statements found that compare an opening window with whole responses are in arXiv:2504.02922, and neither is a plain aligned-versus-base result on harmful prompts. On benign chat prompts, KL between Gemma-2-2b-it and the chat model fed base layer-13 activations is more than three times higher over response tokens 2–10 than over full responses (#f0). #f1 gives KL over the first 9 tokens and over full responses when chat activations are patched only at template-token positions. The pack's only V3 verdict without extracted rows (arXiv:2606.12342: DeepSeek-Math draft and WildJailbreak) rests on string-match refusal, and the checks set it to none. R2 covers the qualitative observation, not a numerical cumulative-KL threshold.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would matched aligned/base pairs, with controlled templates and shared response trajectories, keep a stated majority of cumulative KL within a defined opening window? Would a matched aligned/base pair at 10-100B, or a determinate reasoning-model profile, show the same pattern? Under confidence-based or random decoding, does diffusion-model KL concentrate in the opening response positions, not only in early generation steps? Would pairing positional KL with safety-recovery measurements separate safety-relevant changes from incidental parameter-coupling effects?

source.title: Safety alignment should be made more than just a few tokens deep
source.authors: Xiangyu Qi; Ashwinee Panda; Kaifeng Lyu; Xiao Ma; Subhrajit Roy; Ahmad Beirami; Prateek Mittal; Peter Henderson

original_result.setup: They measured per-token KL divergence between aligned chat models and their base models on harmful HEx-PHI examples.
original_result.result: For Llama-2-7B-Chat and Gemma-7B-IT, KL from the base model is significantly higher in the first few response tokens than in later ones. The result is shown only in a figure, with no numerical values.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: On mixed prompts, aligned-base KL divergence fell; past position ~5, aligned tokens averaged base-model rank <5.
Per-token KL divergence between Llama2 chat and an unsafely fine-tuned model peaked at the first tokens.
In the diffusion language model LLaDA, aligned-base KL peaked at early steps under all decoding orders.
LLaMA2 base and chat distributions differed mainly in roughly the first ten tokens.
Llama-3 aligned-base KL fell from about 1.8 at early response positions to 0.5 at late ones.
Llama-3.1-8B fine-tuned on telecom data diverged from its base model mainly in the first 1–4 tokens.
Mixing aligned-model logits into only the first three tokens raised HarmBench+AdvBench refusal from 27.2% to 89.1%.
On harmful prompts, KL between aligned and unaligned versions of six models concentrated in early positions.
KL between safety-prompted and unprompted Qwen3-0.6B spiked in the first 10 tokens, then decayed after 30.
If each position has separate parameters, theory predicts near-zero KL at positions with negligible harm information.
Mixing aligned-model logits into more tokens kept raising Sorry-Bench refusal: 60.0% at three, 68.2% at twenty.
Theory: when positions share parameters, late-position KL divergence need not track safety-relevant change.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A numerical cumulative-KL test specifying how much divergence lies within a defined opening window.
untested.basis: The original's and the replication's pack lines give figure-only concentration claims. arXiv:2511.12155#r11 gives approximate KL of 1.8 early and 0.5 late (Figure 3 discussion), with no opening-window definition and no cumulative divergence share. The check reads arXiv:2511.12155#r9 and #r11 as cannot_determine for V3 and its V3 verdict as none. Relevant counts keys: versions.V3.rows_by_evidence_form and versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.measurement.

untested.what: The literal aligned-versus-own-pretrained-base claim at toy scale, below 1B, or above 100B.
untested.basis: versions.V3.studies_by_size and versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.measurement.by_size have no toy, <1B or >100B entries. The pack nevertheless includes Qwen3-0.6B at arXiv:2605.15239#P1; its explicit untested-parts line excludes a true aligned/base comparison because the intervention is a system prompt.

untested.what: Aligned-versus-base KL by completed-response position for diffusion language models: none for Dream, and none for LLaDA-Instruct or LLaDA-1.5 under confidence-based or random decoding.
untested.basis: arXiv:2509.23286 explicitly lists Dream KL as unmeasured; its extracted KL rows concern LLaDA. For those rows, the check keeps the V3 supports reading only under left-to-right decoding (arXiv:2509.23286#r16, #r19). It reads the confidence-based rows (#r17, #r20) and random-decoding rows (#r18, #r21) as cannot_determine for V3: they show high early generation-step KL, not concentration in the first positions of the completed response. versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.measurement.by_family groups these models under other or not stated and does not establish Dream coverage.

wording_issues.phrase: mostly in the first few response positions
wording_issues.issue: The records generally describe plotted shapes without cumulative KL mass or a shared opening-window definition. On HEx-PHI, the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct analysis keeps an approximate late KL of 0.5 after about 1.8 early (arXiv:2511.12155#r11). Its adversarial-prefix analysis reports only that KL declines across positions (#r9). Declining KL alone does not establish how much lies within the first few positions. The checker reads #r9 and #r11 as cannot_determine for V3 as worded: neither defines an opening window or gives a cumulative divergence share. It reads the study's V3 supports verdict as none, not as support or a scope limit.

Several results that the verdicts counted as V3 support use other comparators. arXiv:2401.17256 compares Llama2-7B-Chat and Llama2-13B-Chat with the harmfully fine-tuned Unsafe-7B, not their pretrained base, and the 13B pair also crosses sizes (#r2, #r3). Its setup uses 500 samples, at most 256 tokens, and prefixes taken from Unsafe-7B's tokens. Divergence is qualitatively highest at early positions and declines with position (figure-only, no KL values). The checker reads both rows as cannot_determine for the aligned-versus-base comparison and the study's V3 supports verdict as none. arXiv:2605.15239 compares Qwen3-0.6B with a refusal-steering system prompt against the same post-trained model without it (#P1). The subjects in arXiv:2506.00062 are telecom-fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct models, compared with the unaligned base (#r34 to #r36). arXiv:2511.12155#r9 pairs Llama-3.1-8B base with Llama-3-8B-Instruct; the checker confirms the text states this mixed pairing.

The mixed-prompt analysis (1,000 prompts, 20% red-team) does not isolate harmful prompts and gives base and aligned models different templates; its model pair is unstated (arXiv:2312.01552#r4 to #r6). The LLaMA2 base-versus-chat plot covers 100 test samples of unspecified prompt type. It describes differences in roughly the first 10 positions, with no numerical KL values (arXiv:2502.04602#r1). Because those samples are not identified as harmful prompts, the checker reads #r1 as cannot_determine for V3 and the study's V3 supports verdict as none.

The diffusion evidence is indexed by generation step. Under confidence-based or random decoding, early generation steps need not be the opening positions of the completed response. The checker limits the V3 supports verdict for arXiv:2509.23286 to left-to-right decoding (#r16 LLaDA-Instruct, #r19 LLaDA-1.5). It reads the confidence-based and random rows (#r17, #r18, #r20, #r21) as cannot_determine for V3: their high early-step KL does not establish concentration by response position.

The logit-mixing depth experiments measure string-match refusal of an unaligned Llama-3.1-8B draft mixed with a Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct anchor (alpha=0.85, K=3). They do not measure per-token KL between an aligned model and its base. AdvBench refusal is 17.5% at baseline, 92.7% at depth 3 and 97.3% at depth 20 (#R4, #R7). HarmBench-Std (HB-Std) refusal is 13.8% at baseline, 77.8% at depth 3 and 79.6% at depth 20 (#R9, #R12). Sorry-Bench refusal is 10.9% at baseline, 60.0% at depth 3 and 68.2% at depth 20 (#R14, #R17). The checker reads these rows as cannot_determine for V3. It reads all of arXiv:2606.12342's V3 verdicts as none: the supports verdict and the limits_scope verdicts (Sorry-Bench depth sweep; DeepSeek-Math draft and WildJailbreak).

method_sensitivity.what: The pack reports the greatest KL divergence for TSpecLLM fine-tuning, followed by TeleQnA and TeleData, on TeleHarm prompts. The profiles are figure-only; no numeric magnitude comparison is available.

The theoretical near-zero late-KL result (r1) assumes decoupled position parameters and negligible late harm information I_t. With shared parameters (r2), late-position KL can be nonzero through parameter coupling without safety-relevant change. r2 gives no relative magnitude, so it cannot determine whether KL stays mostly within the first few positions (checker: r2 state cannot_determine for V3). This is an analytical dependence, not a measured model sensitivity.

status_amendment.public_note: The scale breakdown now says plainly that no test remains for 10–100B models: the larger-model comparisons in the records do not pair an aligned model with its pretrained base, and the study counts that suggested coverage there were made before the source checks. A new search of the records found nothing that adds to or changes the evidence, so the level stays R2, resting at 1–10B on one independent study whose evidence comes from figures only.
